authors: Hanke FD, Dehnhardt G
title: Aerial visual acuity in harbor seals (Phoca vitulina) as a function of luminance
why: Would give the curve by which a seal's sight in air worsens as light falls, which sets the seal view's light-dependent blur.

authors: Schusterman RJ, Balliet RF
title: Aerial and underwater visual acuity in the California sea lion (Zalophus californianus) as a function of luminance
journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
why: Would give sea lion acuity in air and water across light levels; sea lions hold 26.5% of whale-group records.

authors: Geberl C, Kugler K, Wiegrebe L
title: The spatial resolution of bat biosonar quantified with a visual-resolution paradigm
why: Would set how sharp the bat's echo picture should be, in the same units as visual acuity.

authors: Ordy JM, Samorajski T
title: Visual acuity and ERG-CFF in relation to the morphologic organization of the retina among diurnal and nocturnal primates
why: The only flicker-fusion measurement found for any primate; it would set `rate` for the three primate views.

authors: Silveira LCL, Picanço Diniz CW, Oswaldo-Cruz E
title: Contrast sensitivity function and visual acuity of the opossum
why: Would replace the raccoon view's invented sharpness with a measured opossum value.

authors: Mass AM
title: Visual field organization and retinal resolution in the beluga whale Delphinapterus leucas (Pallas)
why: Would give a toothed whale's field of view, which the dolphin view now leaves unset.

authors: Newman LA, Robinson PR
title: The visual pigments of the West Indian manatee (Trichechus manatus)
why: Would give the manatee's cone peaks, and so the colour model of the manatee view.

authors: Graydon ML, Giorgi PP, Pettigrew JD
title: Vision in flying foxes (Chiroptera: Pteropodidae)
why: Likely holds field, acuity or behaviour for Australian Pteropus, the most recorded bats; it could fill the flying fox view's unset field.

authors: Simmons JA, Kick SA, Lawrence BD, Hale C, Bard C, Escudié B
title: Acuity of horizontal angle discrimination by the echolocating bat, Eptesicus fuscus
why: Would give the big brown bat's angular resolution by sonar, to blur the echo picture sideways.

authors: Griebel U, Schmid A
title: Color vision in the manatee (Trichechus manatus)
why: Behavioural test of manatee colour vision; would confirm or correct the manatee colour row, now resting on a review.

authors: Cowey A, Ellis CM
title: Visual acuity of rhesus and squirrel monkeys
journal: Journal of Comparative and Physiological Psychology
why: Would give a New World monkey's acuity (squirrel monkey) for the capuchin view, now borrowed from the marmoset.

authors: Jacobs GH, Deegan JF, Neitz J, Crognale MA, Neitz M
title: Photopigments and color vision in the nocturnal monkey, Aotus
why: Would give the owl monkey's single cone peak for the lemur view's grey variant.

authors: Bridges CDB, Quilliam TA
title: Visual pigments of men, moles and hedgehogs
why: The only source found on hedgehog pigments; hedgehogs hold 4.6% of mammal-group records and have no measured value.

authors: Melin AD, Danosi CF, McCracken GF, Dominy NJ
title: Dichromatic vision in a fruit bat with diurnal proclivities: the Samoan flying fox (Pteropus samoensis)
why: Would confirm the flying fox colour row in a day-active Pteropus and may give cone peaks.

authors: Danilovich S, Krishnan A, Lee W-J, Borissov IM, Eitan O, Kósa G, Moss CF, Yovel Y
title: Bats regulate biosonar based on the availability of visual information
why: Would set how the echo picture and the eye picture are weighted as light changes.

authors: Lemus K, Meyers R, Ellis S, Belova E, Nichols S, Reagan T, Hastcoat C, Webster C, Smotherman MS
title: Echolocating free-tailed bats use vision and hearing but not magnetoreception when navigating a maze
why: Vision in the Mexican free-tailed bat, the bat recorded most in Alachua; would ground its rows directly.

authors: Rapaport DH, Wilson PD, Rowe MH
title: The distribution of ganglion cells in the retina of the north american opossum (Didelphis virginiana)
why: Would place the Virginia opossum's sharpest area and give an anatomical acuity.

authors: Strobel SM, Moore BA, Freeman KS, Murray MJ, Reichmuth CJ
title: Adaptations for amphibious vision in sea otters (Enhydra lutris): structural and functional observations
why: Sea otters (13,624 records) sit in the mammal group; this would say whether they need the amphibious treatment of the seal view.

authors: White D, Cameron N, Spong P, Bradford J
title: Visual acuity of the killer whale (Orcinus orca)
why: Behavioural acuity of the orca, the second most recorded dolphin, for the dolphin view's sharpness.

authors: Chang HHV, Capshaw G, Skandalis D, Moss CF, Cullen KE
title: Bat eye movements resolve a long-standing question in gaze control
why: Would say whether bats move their eyes, for any gaze effect in the bat view.

authors: Eitan O, Weinberg M, Danilovich S, Barkai Y, Assa R, Yovel Y
title: Functional daylight echolocation in highly visual bats
why: Rousettes in daylight; background for the flying fox view's clicks row.

authors: Winter Y, López J, von Helversen O
title: Ultraviolet vision in a bat
why: Behavioural ultraviolet vision in Glossophaga; background for the bat colour row.

authors: Coimbra JP, Bertelsen MF, Manger PR
title: Retinal ganglion cell topography and spatial resolving power in the river hippopotamus (Hippopotamus amphibius)
why: Another large-mammal acuity and streak for the mammal view.

authors: Kay RF, Kirk EC
title: Osteological evidence for the evolution of activity pattern and visual acuity in primates
why: Background on primate acuity by activity pattern.
